title: Zeytinyagli Enginar
subtitle: Turkish braised artichoke hearts in olive oil and lemon
excerpt: Artichoke hearts braised slowly in olive oil with lemon, dill, and peas until completely tender. A Turkish meze that is always served at room temperature.
sourceNotes: Turkish zeytinyagli tradition, meaning cooked in olive oil. This class of slow-braised vegetable dishes is a cornerstone of Ottoman and Turkish cooking.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make a day ahead and keep covered in the fridge. Remove 30 minutes before serving to bring to room temperature.

content.text: This is a dish that must be eaten at room temperature. The olive oil sets into the braising liquid as it cools and becomes the sauce. Use plenty of lemon and good olive oil as they carry the whole dish.

items.prepNote: juice of all 3, plus zest of 1

content.text: Prepare the artichoke hearts. Snap off the outer leaves until only the pale inner leaves remain. Trim the top third off with a sharp knife. Use a teaspoon to scoop out the hairy choke inside. Immediately rub each heart all over with a cut lemon half and drop into a bowl of cold water mixed with the juice of one lemon. This stops them turning brown.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a wide saute pan over a low to medium heat. Add the onion and carrot and cook gently for 8 minutes until softened but not coloured.

Drain the artichoke hearts and place them flat-side down in the pan between the vegetables. Pour over the remaining olive oil, the juice of the remaining 2 lemons, and 200ml of water. Add the sugar and salt. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and braise over a low heat for 30 to 35 minutes until the artichoke hearts are completely tender when pierced with a knife. Check occasionally and add a splash of water if the pan looks dry.
Add the frozen peas and most of the dill. Cook for 3 minutes more. Remove from the heat.
Leave to cool in the pan for at least 30 minutes. Transfer to a serving dish and spoon over all the pan juices. Scatter over the lemon zest and remaining dill. Serve at room temperature.

items.cause: They were left in the air too long before going into the acidulated water.
items.fix: Work quickly and drop each heart into the lemon water the moment it is trimmed.

items.symptom: The artichokes are tough after braising.
items.cause: They were not cooked long enough, or the heat was too high.
items.fix: Keep the heat low and patient. They need a full 30 to 35 minutes over a very gentle simmer to turn tender.

items.cause: Too much of the fibrous outer leaves remained, or the choke was not fully removed.
items.fix: Trim more aggressively next time. If serving this one, a pinch of extra sugar in the braising liquid can help balance.
